skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Understand basic concepts and legal regulations related to occupational health and safety management.
Comprehend relevant laws and regulations concerning workplace safety and health.
Identify various types of hazards and assess risk levels caused by dangerous factors affecting workers.
Understand macroeconomic, organizational, and individual factors influencing occupational health and safety management.
Understand principles and tools for qualitative and quantitative analysis used to evaluate risks in occupational health and safety management.
Apply theoretical models and research tools to analyze differences between internal and external factors impacting occupational health and safety management.
Analyze real-world scenarios involving occupational accidents and occupational diseases using investigative techniques and necessary tools to ensure a safe and healthy working environment.
Evaluate and predict risk levels from potential hazards within organizations using learned theories and tools.
Demonstrate initiative in learning, researching, and group work.
Select appropriate topics, research methods, and present research findings.
Work effectively in teams on analytical tasks, summarizing, and synthesizing issues related to accident prevention and occupational disease control.
Propose recommendations for occupational health and safety management to government agencies and businesses.
